misconceptions.description: Typing real data straight into the master template file so the blank template is destroyed
misconceptions.trigger: learner opens budget_template.xlsx, fills in their numbers, and saves over it
misconceptions.feedback: Save a copy first (File > Save As, or duplicate the .dotx/.xltx), then edit the copy. The master should stay blank and reusable.

misconceptions.description: Typing a computed result by hand into a spreadsheet cell instead of writing a formula that recalculates
misconceptions.trigger: learner types 450 into a total cell rather than =SUM(B2:B10)
misconceptions.feedback: Use a formula like =SUM(B2:B10) so the total updates when a number changes. A typed 450 goes stale the moment a row edits.

misconceptions.description: Treating a template as a finished document to retype rather than as fixed structure with clearly marked fill-in fields
misconceptions.trigger: learner copies last week's report and edits scattered words, missing some old values
misconceptions.feedback: Mark the variable parts with placeholders like [NAME] or [DATE] so every reuse fills the same fields and nothing stale is left behind.

misconceptions.description: Locking a cell reference with dollar signs when the formula should adjust as it is copied down a column
misconceptions.trigger: learner copies =B2*$C$2 down and every row multiplies by the wrong cell
misconceptions.feedback: Use a relative reference (B2) for the part that should shift per row, and an absolute reference ($C$2) only for the one fixed cell like a tax rate.
